figures.finding: Under fourteen a child's transactions are made for him by his parents, adopters or guardian; from fourteen to eighteen the minor makes them himself with his legal representative's written consent (or its later written approval), but needs no consent to dispose of his own wages and other income or to exercise an author's rights over a work of science, literature or art; a court may, on the parents' or guardianship body's motion, restrict or remove his right to dispose of his earnings; an employment contract with a worker under sixteen is signed by a parent, adopter or guardian. No share of earnings is set aside. The author's-rights rule reaches a young writer or director as an author; an employment contract to write or direct is caught by the same labour rules (reading).

figures.finding: No permit is named: below fourteen a child may work only in creating or performing works in film, sport, theatre, concert organisations, circus, television or radio; under sixteen only on a temporary contract that doesn't impede compulsory schooling, signed by a parent or guardian. Hours beyond school time: under seven up to two a day and four a week; seven to twelve (as the text reads) three, at most six a week; twelve to fifteen four a day and twelve a week; fifteen to sixteen twenty-four a week; sixteen to eighteen thirty-six a week; no one under eighteen works at night (22:00 to 06:00). The under-fourteen exception names 'creating' works as well as performing them, so it reaches a child writer or director employed by such an organisation (reading).

value.creativeWorkUnder14: cinema, sports, theatre, concert organisations, circus, television, radio
value.under16: temporary contract only, no impediment to compulsory education

figures.applies: Labour Code arts. 17.1, 140, 148 (as amended to 4 December 2024).

sources.said: 2. Persons under the age of fourteen may be involved only in creating or performing compositions (creative work) in cinematographic, sports, theatrical or concert organisations, circus, television or radio. 3. A temporary employment contract shall be concluded with persons under the age of sixteen. Admitting persons under the age of sixteen for permanent employment shall be prohibited. Persons under the age of sixteen may, in the cases and under the procedure prescribed by this Code, be admitted for temporary employment, unless it impedes their compulsory education process. ... (1) children under the age of seven — up to two hours a day, but not more than four hours during the week, beyond the hours set for mandatory education; (2) children between the ages of seven and twelve — up to three hours a week, but not more than six hours during the week, beyond the hours set for mandatory education; (3) children between the ages of twelve and fifteen — up to four hours a day, but not more than twelve hours during the week, beyond the hours set for mandatory education; ... (4) children between the ages of fifteen and sixteen — up to 24 hours a week, beyond the hours set for mandatory education; (5) employees between the ages of sixteen and eighteen — up to 36 hours a week, beyond the hours set for mandatory education; ... 1. Night time shall be considered the period between 22:00 and 6:00. ... 3. Persons under the age of eighteen (except for the cases prescribed by part 3.1 of this Article) as well as employees who are not allowed to be employed in night work according to a medical conclusion are not allowed to be engaged in night work.

figures.finding: Full capacity comes at eighteen; a minor of sixteen who works under an employment contract or, with his parents' or guardian's consent, runs a business may be declared fully capable (emancipation) by the guardianship body, or by a court where they don't consent; from sixteen a minor may be a member of a cooperative. Whether a minor may be a participant or director of a limited-liability company wasn't read from the company law.

value.emancipationBy: guardianship and trusteeship body with the parents' consent, or a court
